coordinate_frame: Selenographic planetocentric, Mean Earth/Polar Axis, longitude east-positive
disclaimer: Points are illustrative locations on or near named south-polar features. Coordinates are approximate and are NOT official Artemis landing-region definitions. Verify against the IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature and LOLA products before scientific use.

sites.name: Shackleton–de Gerlache Connecting Ridge
sites.description: Elevated ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters, frequently discussed in the literature for its long periods of illumination.
sites.coordinate_note: Approximate point on the ridge crest (~222.7°E), taken from published illumination studies; verify before use.

sites.name: Peak Near Shackleton
sites.description: Massif on the far side of Shackleton crater as seen from Earth; an example of a high-standing site with a low local horizon.
sites.coordinate_note: Approximate summit area; verify before use.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim
sites.description: Point on the rim of de Gerlache crater, on the Earth-facing side of the pole.
sites.coordinate_note: Approximate rim location; de Gerlache crater centre is near 88.5°S, 87°W.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.description: Large massif near the 0° meridian, facing Earth; a candidate for steadier direct-to-Earth line of sight than sites on the far-side-facing slopes.
sites.coordinate_note: Approximate summit area; verify before use.

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.description: Flat-topped mountain (formerly Leibnitz β); the IM-2 lander targeted its plateau in 2025.
